text:
Olivia: quick design q — we've been seeing short lived tail-latency spikes when large customer bursts hit the edge shapers. thinking about a lightweight 'propagation credit' that moves with the ingress request, decays across zones, and temporarily relaxes local shaping to avoid oscillation. any immediate red flags?

Matt: interesting. is this more like a cross-zone reservoir (global credit) or a per-ingress sticky credit that follows the client?

Olivia: per-ingress sticky credit. idea: when a client ramps up, the first few requests get a small boost credit (short TTL) that lets them burst across a couple of front-door nodes without tripping local fair-shed heuristics. credit decays multiplicatively every 5s.

Sara: curious about safety — wont this let a misbehaving tenant bypass quota briefly? how do we tie it to abuse signals?

Olivia: tie it to tenant score + a cap. i.e., only tenants under an abuse threshold get the sticky credit. and the credit magnitude is bounded by a fraction of their normal token allowance.

Tyler: how does this interact with Dedicated vs Hosted customers? Dedicated pools currently have stricter per-gpu admission — we shouldn't let credits cross capacity domains.

Olivia: agree — credits are scoped to ingress domain. they do NOT move across capacity tiers. propagation only across front-door replicas in same region/pool class.

Matt: can you sketch config? something like:

```
prop_credit:
  enabled: true
  initial_tokens: 200  # token-equivalent burst
  decay_half_life_s: 10
  max_fraction_of_quota: 0.05
  abuse_score_threshold: 0.7
  scope: regional_frontdoor
```

Sara: ok. telemetry question — we need to be able to see when credits are applied and their effect on observed SLOs. otherwise we'll be flying blind.

Olivia: plan is to emit a short annotation in the trace and a metric `prop_credit.applied{zone,tenant}` with the amount and remaining ttl. also tag request logs with `prop_credit=true` so we can quickly slice latency percentiles.

Tyler: what about fairness impacts? if many clients simultaneously get credit, we reintroduce burst contention. maybe stagger issuance with tiny jitter and a local cap per-node.

Matt: +1 to jitter. also consider a backoff feedback: if node latency rises above a threshold while credits are active, throttle future credit grants for a cooldown window.

Olivia: exactly — credit grants are conditional: node-level health check + tenant score + per-node active-credit-cap. grant logic pseudo:

```
if node_ok && tenant_score < abuse_threshold && node_active_credit < cap:
  grant_credit(tenant, min(initial_tokens, quota * max_fraction))
else:
  deny_credit()
```

ingress-bot: [monitor] node frontdoor-eu-3: 2023-11-02T14:03:11Z latency spike detected (p50 45ms -> p99 430ms), applied emergency shed.

Sara: good to have that emergency path. question: should this be an adaptive feature behind an experiment flag first? i think we need a staged rollout (canary per region, then soft launch with telemetry-driven auto-disable).

Olivia: yes staged rollout. propose: canary 5% traffic eu-west for 48h, collect `p99_latency`, `credit_applied_rate`, `error_rate`, and `quota_overrun_alerts`. auto-rollback if p99 increases > 20% or error_rate increases.

Tyler: owner? i'll volunteer to pair on infra changes for per-node caps and the health checks.

Matt: i'll take the telemetry dashboards + experiment gating alerts.

Sara: i'll do the security/abuse scoring integration and add tests for exploit scenarios.

Olivia: awesome. i'll write a short RFC/spike doc capturing grant logic + config + rollout plan. aim to have initial draft by EOD tomorrow.

Matt: tiny nit — make sure this integrates with our tracing flags. we need to correlate `prop_credit` with KV-cache hit rates and batch sizes.

Olivia: noted. action items: Olivia -> RFC draft, Tyler -> infra caps + health check, Matt -> dashboards & tracing slices, Sara -> abuse scoring + tests. will post RFC link here when ready. :+1:
